doc.title: Joanne Brackeen interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 10, 2001

title: Her composing process and attitude to the present
summary: Ideas arrive as feeling before she reaches the piano; she feels the world has caught up with her and still writes by pen.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well suppose I wanted to commission you for a new piece of music. And I basically said, “Whatever you want.” How do you start the process?
Oh I have a lot of ideas. Whatever you want, that’s a pretty big field there. I’d think about it and, you know—
Do you get ideas away from the piano?

Well the ideas come like in a form of energy that doesn’t have a form. It’s like a feel. And then I go to the piano and it comes out. That’s how I translate it. But it’s there before I go to the piano. However, the piano is such a great translator, almost equal to going on- line on the computer. How could you get on-line without the computer? That’s how the piano is for me. It’s like it really makes things very easy. So I write from the piano. But it’s already written before I get to the piano.
Interesting. You have a rhythmic feel perhaps?
Well it’s hard to define it. It’s the whole thing.
You seem to be someone who is always searching for something new to me.

Yeah. I was thinking in the taxi on the way up here, I’m really happy I’m living in these times now. Because I’ve always been kind of like that, and now the outside world is as crazy as I was on the inside, and I feel good. I feel like really more at home.
It is. Yeah. It certainly is.
The world caught up with you.
With whatever it was in me, I don’t know.
Are you a technical oriented person.
No. But I don’t have anything against it.
You still like to write your music with a pen?

I do. I have the computer now that will work that way easily, I just got it last week so I probably will end up having to do it the other way, that’s for sure. But naturistically yeah, I like to just write it out.
